best_weapons.commentary_details: Lynae's Signature weapon provides her with a significant boost to her ATK, CRIT Rate and Basic Attack DMG Bonus, while increasing all damage dealt by the team when applying Tune Rupture or Tune Strain. example_teams.team_notes: Lynae & Mornye can go with close to any damage dealer, only exceptions being Zani & Cartethyia.
Hiyuki can get close to Aemeath teams in power thanks to Chisa and Hiyuki's super high base damage. However, Aemeath on Fusion Burst in this team is much weaker than the Rupture team we listed above.
Ciaccona is also an option for the third slot alongside Iuno in specific.

cons: Low headroom for Swap Cancels, very Intro-dependent, and major abilities have long cooldowns - locked into doing one rotation with relatively low flexibility, though quickswap with Lynae isn't fully impossible.
pros: The best generalist Hybrid buffer in the game, with tons of universal buffs to a single character while dealing a much higher amount of personal damage than most Hybrids;
Doesn't need her Signature weapon to perform - very F2P friendly;

Functions in almost all teams in the game and is the best buffer for a good chunk of them, pushing all Liberation damage dealers way up into the meta, with some specialized Tune Rupture/Strain synergies to boot (as well as other old DPS to an extent).

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Lynae is a 5-star Spectro Pistol Hybrid buffer who specializes in... not much, actually. Well, that's only partially true, but if you're familiar at all with Lynae, you should know she is quite the generalist buffer, and she's super good in that role. It's difficult to overstate her team flexibility and efficiency, as aside from certain characters who are overly reliant on one specific partner (Lupa for most Fusion characters, Ciaccona for Cartethyia, Phoebe for Zani for example), Lynae quite literally buffs everybody and does a fantastic job at it, having a solid amount of personal damage on top. She has specialties in Tune Rupture, Tune Strain, and Liberation DMG that can provide even better synergies than her standard generalist use cases. While all this won't make her the best Main DPS, in her role of a secondary buffer, she can provide a lot of value to most accounts, as long as she's played properly, and there's no better way to make sure of that than understanding her kit in full, which we will cover below:

sections.heading: Key Mechanics
paragraphs: Lynae is a character with 3 Forte resources she needs to manage: Overflow, Lumiflow and True Color. Overflow is mostly replenished by her Intro and either a couple of Basic Attacks or a single Skill. Fully building up Overflow allows her to cast a charged Basic Attack called Spark Collision, which then switches her to her Lumiflow state. Lumiflow replenishes over time with no way to boost its generation, but it is also fully replenished by holding Spark Collision to its maximum stage (which requires a few seconds of charging time). Once she has 40 Lumiflow, she can cast a Jump attack called Polychrome Leap. Finally, for each Polychrome Leap, she gains 1 point of True Color up to 3, which are used to cast her big Forte Mid-Air Attack, Visual Impact. This always concludes her rotation.

This essentially covers her gameplay. Beyond everything listed above, her Ultimate has two parts, but only the first one is worth executing since it deals almost all of the damage and doesn't cost any time while still providing buffs. It will be cast after Intro to ensure buff uptime.

sections.heading: Who does Lynae buff & How?
paragraphs: Lynae can apply the following buffs to characters on her team:
With her Outro: 15% all-type DMG Amplification and 25% Liberation DMG Amplification to the next character via Outro (expires on swap);
With her Ultimate: 24% party-wide all-type DMG Bonus;
Upon casting Visual Impact: 40 points of Tune Break Boost party-wide (this boosts Tune Break-related damage);
With her Echo set: a total of 30% ATK and 10% all-type DMG Bonus to the next character via Outro;
With her Signature weapon: up to 24% party-wide all-type DMG Bonus.

This totals to 58% DMG Bonus, 30% ATK, 15% All-type and 25% Liberation DMG Amplification to one character. Even without her Signature weapon factored in, on Static Mist (one of the permanent banner Pistols) she trades off 24% DMG Bonus for 10% ATK, which is a negligible loss in team damage.

You may have realized that every single one of Lynae's buffs are very generally applicable, other than her Liberation DMG Amplification on Outro. Even without this factored in, Lynae stands out as our first ever generalist Hybrid buffer, capable of buffing almost any Main DPS in the game. Alongside universal Supports like Shorekeeper and especially Mornye, Lynae makes for the strongest universal buffing core in the game, capable of interacting with and improving almost any Main DPS's damage ceiling by highly significant amounts.

sections.heading: Resonance Mode: What does it do? What to use in what teams?
paragraphs: Lynae has 2 modes that she can switch between freely in her Forte page out of combat. This means in combat, only 1 of the 2 modes will be available. They are each related to Tune Break: Lynae is indeed capable, via most of her essential attacks, of applying Tune Rupture or Tune Strain, which are her 2 modes. Tune Rupture acts as an extra instance of damage on every Tune Break skill cast, while Tune Strain is an extra DMG Taken increase to characters who can respond to it. Mornye is one such character, as she can deal Tune Rupture damage of her own and benefit from the damage increase of Tune Strain, depending on which one Lynae applies for her.

As for which one to use: If a direct Tune Strain synergy is in the team (as in, the Main DPS relies on it e.g Luuk), then use Tune Strain. Otherwise, always go for Tune Rupture. The overall raw damage increase Lynae gets from Tune Rupture damage is huge, so it's always best if Tune Strain response isn't on the Main DPS, and if the Main DPS interacts with Tune Rupture directly (e.g Aemeath), then you should be using Tune Rupture mode anyways.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: If it wasn't obvious by everything we've stated in this review so far, Lynae is one of the strongest meta presences that we've ever seen. As the queen of team flexibility in the Hybrid role while still being even stronger in her specialized Liberation, Tune Rupture and Tune Strain buffing capabilities, even without a specific DPS to associate with Lynae, remains a top-tier meta contender, and it's by a landslide too. This level of flexibility and general strength in Hybrids is, to put it bluntly, never before seen. Her specific synergies are with some of the strongest meta contenders as well, including but not limited to Aemeath, Luuk, Hiyuki and Iuno.

To mention her top team, alongside Aemeath and Mornye, she makes for one of the strongest single-target focused teams in the game, on the level of all the most recent DPS. And that's only one of her many teams.

But that's not all: Lynae functions very well with a myriad of already successful DPS characters like Carlotta, Phoebe, and Camellya, as well as serving as a perfectly viable replacement to the already established partners to DPS powerhouses like Augusta and even Phrolova, the current best DPS in the game when factoring in all endgame content.

In conclusion, Lynae is one of the strongest characters Wuthering Waves has ever seen. As we said in the intro to this review, it's difficult to overstate her team flexibility, and she appears as one of the strongest contenders in the meta, capable of working exceptionally well with practically any DPS out there with some specialized modern synergies that only accentuate her value further. Reminiscent of Shorekeeper in universality, but as a Hybrid buffer instead, Lynae is easily one of the best Hybrid buffers in the game, with only a bright future to come as more Liberation damage dealers, or Tune Rupture/Tune Strain-related characters release in the future.

synergies.commentary: Lynae pairs best with Liberation damage dealers who can make full use of her Outro. Aemeath is by far the best choice, she perfectly synergizes with every element of Lynae's kit and makes for an overwhelmingly strong team composition. While Hiyuki doesn't have full synergy with Lynae, paired with Chisa the team can match Aemeath in power. Iuno is also a really strong character in this role too, dealing a ton of Liberation damage. In fact, Lynae buffs Iuno so well that it's enough to make her one of the best singletarget DPS characters in the game; however Lynae is also one of the premium choices for yangyang-xuanling even if her Outro isn't fully taken advantage of, by virtue of her generalist buffs alone.

Lynae is the best generalist Hybrid character in the game, and this means she's also the best buffer for quite a lot of characters that wouldn't immediately come to mind. Phoebe as a DPS doesn't have any dedicated partners but Lynae is perfect for her since general buffs are what she wants to cover her numerous damage types; Carlotta and Camellya on the other hand already have dedicated buffers but their kits don't provide as much buffing strength as Lynae, which can make her slightly better when properly built for damage.

These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice generally. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.
